_note: Measured FP baseline. Counts may only DECREASE. Raising a number requires a documented justification in the same commit.
_generated_by: scripts/fp-report.cjs, via the harness in tests/security-fp-corpus.test.cjs. Counts are measured, never hand-authored.
_entropy_note: Entropy findings route to findings[] and never to blocked[], so they are advisory only and cannot hard-block an import or fail CI. Asserted by tests/security-fp-corpus.test.cjs. Threshold is H > 5.5 (security.cjs).
_entropy_metric: Entropy counts are measured at stride 1 over every window alignment (scripts/fp-report.cjs, peakEntropyAnyAlignment), NOT from the detector's STEP-aligned windows. The detector still samples every 128 chars in production; only the budget measurement is alignment-invariant, so that inserting bytes anywhere in a file cannot move a borderline entry across the threshold and fail CI on an unrelated edit. Content shorter than one window is scored whole, matching the detector. KNOWN GAP: partial tail windows of longer content are excluded, because their length is a function of total content length — the same instability in another form. The detector does scan that tail, so an FP whose only high-entropy region sits in the final <256 chars is invisible to this budget. A 64-char tail can reach H=6.0 while diluting to nothing inside a 256-char window, so this is a real one-sided blind spot, accepted in exchange for a count that does not move on unrelated edits.

entropy_fp.raised_justification: Not a regression — the metric changed. This count was previously measured from the detector's own STEP-aligned windows, which made it a function of byte offset rather than of content: inserting 7 blank bytes at the top of an otherwise untouched commands.cjs moved it across the threshold, because the 256-char window re-aligned over the pre-existing YAML_TIMESTAMP block at line ~711. Any edit above a dense region could flip the count, so the budget is now measured by scripts/fp-report.cjs at stride 1 (peakEntropyAnyAlignment) — the peak over all alignments, which no byte shift can change. On this corpus that reports 3 files where the anchored measurement reported 1. It is NOT a general upper bound on the detector: partial tail windows are excluded (see _entropy_metric), and a file whose only high-entropy region is a short tail is flagged by the detector but not counted here. All three files were verified present at the unmodified HEAD (f022bf6) under the new metric with the same max_H values; commands.cjs reports a shifted window (19029 at HEAD) only because this change edits that file. Entropy routes to findings[] and can never block an import or fail CI.
